All declarations are complete definitions or generated record/typeclass infrastructure. admissible contains analytic and approved operational assumptions, never the expected-clock inequality or accuracy conclusion. successful is a visible conjunction of integrability, one-point accuracy and a time bound. Its inequalities are goals for later Convergence proofs, not established by defining the setup.

PrimitiveService retains jointly measurable exact matching completions at finite actual times, on a common full-measure tape event for legal requests, with idle None behavior. The unchanged batchScheduleIndependent provider imposes conditional independence of indexed difference-batch durations/ties from fresh assigned labels under the raw seed law times O.law. It does not assume completed IID, the desired clock estimate or accuracy. This is the user-approved stronger premise recorded in the adaptation ledger. Private-row freshness, history properties, completed-label IID and conditional invocation-cost bounds must still be proved. The analytic lower/gap and three smoothness clauses match the previously reviewed parallel setup. The added large-sample inequality is explicitly required in source Theorem5; it was not imposed on the separate iteration-only interface.

Writing A=Lminus+Lpm*sqrt((1-rho)/(rho*S)), the displayed clock bound is exactly 12*t(m)+(48*Delta/epsilon)*A*(rho*t(m)+(1-rho)*t(S)). The real nonnegative coefficient and probability weights are embedded into ENNReal; valid makes each nonnegative, so ofReal does not truncate a needed signed term. Clock expectation is the nonnegative lintegral of output.2, allowing an infinite expectation/bound without a false totalized Bochner-integral claim. The gradient integrability conjunct concerns only output.1. The source gap is bounded above by the supplied Delta; valid makes the resulting coefficient monotone in that substitution. Neither a missing factor of two in paired gradients nor the discarded final refresh is assumed away by the formula; these costs require the explicit later collection/prefix arguments. Rechecked the source 12 and 48 constants, actual coefficient Lminus+Lpm*sqrt((1-rho)/(rho*S)), and mixture rho*t(m)+(1-rho)*t(S). S remains arbitrary positive; largeSample is explicit and tau remains hidden from publicInput.

The accepted freeTime factory returns (x0,0) for Delta=0 or Lminus=0; otherwise it runs FreyaPage.prefix on familyRaw publicInput true. That record computes eta and K from problem data and epsilon. Prefix rounds are K-1, while the independent output selector still ranges over the K points x0,...,x(K-1). The underlying output is (state.selected,state.clock); initialization starts clock at zero, collector completions update it from actual returned times, and halted idle calls preserve it. The setup independence premise uses the same true-prefix raw record. Same-point law transport and the expected-clock proof remain outstanding. In the nonstationary branch C=2*Delta*A/epsilon is positive and K=max 1 ceil C gives K-1<=C. This avoids adding an uncontrolled arbitrary-S final refresh to the source coefficient. Initialization remains part of the actual prefix clock and is covered by the first term. Current raw independence premise uses prefix=true, matching freeTime and its K-1 rounds. The output point is selected from K points, while elapsed time is the actual returned clock; literal final-refresh time is not silently identified with prefix time.

The interface implements the accepted general-S time-to-output interpretation of source Theorem5. It retains the source analytic and large-sample assumptions and the expressly approved operational schedule/label-independence departure. The output is one selected point paired with the actual finite nonnegative clock. Success displays expected squared-gradient accuracy and the explicit source expected-time expression. It uses the prefix factory rather than asserting that the same displayed bound covers a rounded arbitrary-S literal final refresh. A natural primitive completion-event budget belongs to the later public theorem and is distinct from the ENNReal wall-clock bound in successful. This setup-only packet has no public budget/result row; actual output transport, accuracy, time and event-budget proofs are still required.

Output is Space d times NNReal, with a selected point and actual elapsed completion clock, not a trajectory or an equilibrium-time surrogate. equilibriumTime appears only in the deterministic bound. ENNReal casts preserve the finite clock and make expected-time statements meaningful at zero/infinite advertised worker bounds. The explicit flat Params and Family reconstruction preserve the dimensions and hidden analysis data.

Reused unchanged accepted primitive service, independence, familyRaw, prefix execution and tuning evidence, checking the actual true-prefix application. The familyRaw and freeTime compiler identities match their accepted tuning records. Retrieved and canonical-hash-verified this spec/publicInput/freeTime records, and inspected the accepted PAGE output and clock-update definitions. Generated spec facts are Euclidean completeness and numeral AtLeastTwo instances for 12 and 48; no runtime conclusion is hidden in them.

The sole consumer is FreeTime, with the source-to-prefix interpretation explicitly recorded in its graph and approved design. Native statement gates passed before this review. The current setup has no budget/result and hence no catalog row; later public and composition gates must inspect its actual extracted budget, rendered time/accuracy interface and execution correspondence. This does not approve the displayed bound for a different literal final-refresh algorithm. Fresh queue bytes/hash/basis and exact current source/compiler/provider identities were validated. The global helper-name repair alters no setup clause or consumer. Public catalog and budget gates remain due at the wrapper.

S>m is allowed and is the reason the prefix interpretation matters. K=1 still performs initialization, selects x0 and has zero subsequent rounds; the initial clock term covers it. Delta=0 or Lminus=0 uses (x0,0), requiring the stationary-return lemma. rho=1 correctly eliminates the inactive difference-time term, including 0*infinity in ENNReal. Zero and all-infinite tau bounds remain allowed; no infinity/infinity ratio is formed, and an infinite advertised bound does not invent a completion for an environment that never finishes.
